text:
maya: Quick design review request — noticed in staging when sending 30 invites rapidly the invite drawer shows mixed CTA states after flipping the org SSO enforcement. I attached a short recording.

arjun: can you repro steps?

maya: Steps: 1) Org > People > Invite, 2) paste 30 emails, 3) Send invites, 4) flip org SSO enforcement ON while queue is processing. Result: some rows show 'Resend' while the top toast says 'All invites sent'.

kat: repro'd here. UI state mismatch — backend returns per-invite partial errors but the drawer flips to success unconditionally. Two quick UX options: show per-row micro-status OR keep top-level in processing until all callbacks done.

sam: agree. accessibility nit: the rows that flip to 'Resend' are not announced by screen readers. missing aria-live on the status cell.

olivia: copy nit: prefer 'Retry invite' over 'Resend' — clearer for admins (avoids implication of duplicate emails).

designbot: Proposed approaches:
- A) Disable SSO toggle while invites are processing with a tooltip explaining why.
- B) Allow toggle but surface a persistent banner: 'Processing invites — toggling SSO may affect pending invites' with a link to more info.
- C) Let toggle apply immediately, keep queue semantics, and surface per-row errors with contextual tooltips and a clear final audit entry.

arjun: leaning toward B. Blocking a security toggle is product-negative. Also: we should write an audit-log event that ties toggle timestamp to the invite batch (customers will need the correlation).

maya: UX action list: 1) add aria-live to invite-row status, 2) update CTA copy to 'Retry invite', 3) add processing banner with link to audit-log entry, 4) ensure aggregate state reflects per-row results (no optimistic global success). I'll push a Figma patch and short proto.

kat: layout nit: when the banner appears the drawer height shifts and focus jumps. Keep drawer scroll height stable; animate banner in without reflowing content.

sam: dev note: API already emits per-invite callback events (status: processing, delivered, failed). We can stream these over websocket to the client to update rows in place and keep top-level status until the final batch callback. That should prevent false success toasts.

olivia: accessibility follow-up: ensure the banner has role="status" and aria-live="polite" and is reachable by keyboard. Also ensure per-row error details are keyboard-expandable.

maya: tagging @arjun @sam for engineering bandwidth. Can we get a spike this week and a prototype by next sprint?

arjun: i'll take the spike. ETA: EOD Friday for a demo.

sam: will prep websocket hooks and a small test dataset for bulk invites.

maya: thanks all — i'll post Figma and copy updates in this thread shortly :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder — staging deploy scheduled 2026-03-27 09:00 UTC. Changes after that need merge PRs.

olivia: ack.
